question: What is the current release of the Human Protein Atlas, what new data did it add, and how many antibodies and human genes does the atlas cover in this release?

tool_uses.name: web_search
tool_uses.input: {"query":"Human Protein Atlas latest release new data antibodies human genes release"}

turns.text:
The Human Protein Atlas’ current listed release is **version 25.1**, dated **25 May 2026**. It adds:

- **Deep Visual Proteomics (DVP)** to the Single Cell resource: MS-based protein profiles for **27 cell-type shapes** across **14 tissues** (classified into 24 cell types), with matched single-cell RNA data and RNA–protein agreement/specificity measures. [Release history](https://www.proteinatlas.org/about/releases#25.1)
- **Bulk-tissue quantitative MS proteomics** in the Tissue resource: data for **20 tissue types** and protein profiles for **more than 12,700 genes**. [Release history](https://www.proteinatlas.org/about/releases#25.1)

The version 25.1 notes do **not** state a new total number of antibodies or total atlas-wide human-gene coverage. The immediately preceding major release (v25.0) reports the atlas as containing **over 27,800 antibodies**, targeting proteins encoded by **over 17,400 human genes** (about **88%** of human protein-coding genes). [Release history](https://www.proteinatlas.org/about/releases#25.0)
